`ignoreErrors`/`denyUrls`/inbound filters consider known noise

`featureFlagsIntegration` + webhook

Console output is stored where the policy `cloudflare.owner` says: Workers Logs (`observability`) or Sentry Logs (`consoleLoggingIntegration`, `Sentry.logger`), both only when the policy says `both`; an unset policy is a decision finding, never a guess

applies_when: Cloudflare unit with Sentry tracing or `observability.traces`
passes_when: One trace system per request path as the policy says (`split`: Sentry traces, Cloudflare traces off; `otlp`: Sentry tracing off in the Worker and export on; `both` accepts two)
`persist` is set on purpose: false when the destination (for example Sentry) should be the only store, because persisted data is stored and, from 2026-12-01, counted by Cloudflare
One paging owner for Worker errors (Cloudflare Issues automations or Sentry alerts) unless the policy says `both`

applies_when: an edge whose client or server has Sentry
passes_when: Per edge: the client sends `sentry-trace` and `baggage` to the server origin (browser: `tracePropagationTargets` lists it; React Native and Node default to all requests), the server SDK continues the trace, and a browser to cross-origin edge has CORS allowing both headers

applies_when: an edge whose target unit has no Sentry
passes_when: A client that sends trace headers reaches a unit with Sentry present, or the half trace is a recorded decision

applies_when: two or more units with Sentry
passes_when: (a) The same deployment stage has the same `environment` spelling in every unit; (b) one deploy can be matched across units by a shared release value. File the two halves as separate findings

applies_when: two units with the same DSN
passes_when: Units that build and release separately (own source maps, own release) have their own Sentry project, or the shared project is deliberate
